name: Geese
label: Partisan Records
lede: Geese started as schoolmates running through a Tame Impala cover in a Fort Greene basement. Nine years later the New Yorker and NME both put Getting Killed at the top of their 2025 lists.

eras.title: A basement in Fort Greene
eras.text: Schoolmates in Brooklyn practice in Max Bassin's Fort Greene basement and self-release three records they've since pulled from streaming. College almost ends it.

years.h: The first song they play together is a Tame Impala cover
years.p: Cameron Winter, Emily Green, Dominic DiGesu and Max Bassin meet at Brooklyn Friends School and the Park Slope Rock School, and the cover is Tame Impala's "Mind Mischief".
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band practiced and recorded in Bassin's Fort Greene basement. The name comes from Green's childhood nickname, Goose.

years.p: An untitled EP lands April 21, then the album A Beautiful Memory on July 13. Neither is on streaming services now.

years.h: Bottomless Pink Lagoon adds a second guitarist
years.p: Foster Hudson joins on guitar and the band self-releases the EP on August 18. He stays through 2023, and the EP is off streaming too.

eras.title: A SoundCloud link, then Partisan
eras.text: A manager hears a SoundCloud upload, labels start circling, and the debut arrives with a sound that turns heads.

years.src: Wikipedia: Emily Green · Wikipedia: Projector · Wikipedia: Cameron Winter
years.h: A manager hears a SoundCloud upload and the labels call
years.p: Willie Upbin starts pitching the band around in 2020, and Geese sign with Partisan Records. Winter skips Boston University to keep going.
years.xp:
The band had been close to breaking up over college. The demos drew interest from 4AD, Fat Possum and Sub Pop before Partisan won.

Wikipedia's Projector page says the record was first uploaded to SoundCloud, where Upbin found it. The band picked Partisan because they saw it as "the best of the worst" among labels.

q: It was this transcendental moment where we were all really in the zone.
yt: KEXP at Home session, Projector era
years.h: Projector comes out of a basement they called the Nest
years.p: Recorded in Bassin's basement studio from late 2019 into early 2020 and mixed by Dan Carey. Pitchfork gave it 6.6.
years.xp:
"Disco" premiered on Apple Music 1 on June 22, 2021, ahead of the October 29 release. Metacritic lists 83 from eight reviews, and NME called it one of the year's most thrilling rock debuts.

Winter told Apple Music 1's Matt Wilkinson about the session where it clicked.

eras.title: Jam band, sort of
eras.text: Sam Revaz joins on keys, James Ford produces, and the songs stretch out. Then a guitarist leaves for school.

years.h: 3D Country is where the post-punk kids start jamming
years.p: James Ford produces at the Diamond Mine in Queens, and Pitchfork's Brady Gerber gives it 6.8, hearing a band with newfound dynamics and space.
years.xp: Four singles come first: "Cowboy Nudes", "3D Country", "Mysterious Love" and "I See Myself". The 4D Country EP follows on October 13 with four more tracks from the same sessions. Metacritic shows 78 from six reviews.

years.cap: Geese at Bar Ritz PDB, Montreal
years.h: Foster Hudson leaves to focus on school
years.p: Hudson steps out after 3D Country and its EP. Geese carry on as four, with Sam Revaz on keys when they tour.

eras.title: Winter goes solo, Geese go live
eras.text: Geese open for bigger bands and put out a live album, and Winter's solo record widens the audience before the next Geese record.

years.cap: Geese at White Oak Music Hall, Houston, May 5, 2024
years.h: A live album before the next studio one
years.p: Alive & in Person arrives on Partisan June 28, while Geese open for Greta Van Fleet and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Green came out publicly through the release. Green also has a side project, Star's Revenge, with Sunflower Bean drummer Olive Faber.

years.h: Winter goes solo with a piano and a baritone
years.p: Heavy Metal carries Cameron Winter's name well past Geese. Pitchfork ranked it No. 3 of 2025 and named "Love Takes Miles" the best song.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports Nick Cave called Winter's vocals "glorious", and that the New York Times' Lizzy Goodman described it as received as a tour de force.

eras.title: Getting Killed
eras.text: Ten days in Los Angeles with Kenny Beats in the room produce the record the critics pile onto.

years.h: Ten days at Putnam Hill, with Los Angeles on fire
years.p: Winter on making Getting Killed with Kenny Beats in January, about fourteen hours a day as wildfires hit Southern California.
years.xp:
The band met Kenny Beats (Kenneth Blume) at Austin City Limits in October 2024 and sketched demos at Putnam Hill that November. They arrived in January with about twenty unfinished songs.

Thirty-minute jams built on repeating grooves became the base, with bass and drums tracked over and over. Wikipedia's page on "Taxes" says the band co-produced with Kenny Beats.

years.h: "Taxes" ends in a mosh pit that eats itself
years.p: Noel Paul's video starts as live footage and ends in cannibal chaos. Geese play the song on Jimmy Kimmel Live! from Brooklyn on October 1.
years.xp: NME and Stereogum both ranked the song No. 2 for 2025, Pitchfork No. 10, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Getting Killed · Wikipedia: Cameron Winter
years.h: Pitchfork's 9.0, and the year-end lists fall in line
years.p: Best New Music, then No. 7 on Pitchfork's 2025 list. Sam Sodomsky called it the band's strangest and strongest work.
years.xp:
Metacritic lists 89 from 19 reviews. The Guardian, NME, AllMusic and Mojo gave it five stars; Exclaim! gave it 6/10. The New Yorker and NME put it first for 2025, Stereogum tied for first, and Rolling Stone had it fifth. It reached No. 96 on the Billboard 200, No. 26 in the UK and No. 1 on the UK independent chart.

On the cover, Green stands in a white dress with a trumpet in one hand and a revolver pointed at the camera in the other. Two records earlier, Pitchfork had given the band 6.6 and then 6.8.

years.h: Winter headlines Carnegie Hall, and Paul Thomas Anderson films it
years.p: Wikipedia calls him one of the youngest artists to play the room. Benny Safdie assisted on the shoot.

years.h: Geese make their Saturday Night Live debut
years.p: They play "Au Pays du Cocaine" and "Trinidad", both from Getting Killed.
years.xp: Billboard and Rolling Stone covered the debut. "Trinidad", the album's opener, runs in an unusual 13/8 time signature.

years.h: Fourth in the BBC's Sound of 2026, then a Brit
years.p: Geese win International Group of the Year at the 2026 Brit Awards, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Wired traces campaigns for Geese to their PR firm
years.p: Wired reports on April 14 that Chaotic Good Projects ran campaigns for Winter and Geese, and co-founder Adam Tarsia confirms the firm engineered them.
years.xp: Wired's headline was "The Fanfare Around the Band Geese Actually Was a Psyop", by John Semley. Musician Eliza McLamb, whose Substack post prompted the story, said she does not consider Geese a "psy-op". Other writers argued the tactics are common.
